Machick 2, developed by Deadpixel and published by Nuntius Games and Vsoo Games, is an electrifying sequel that amplifies the unique blend of frantic action, quirky humor, and deep customization that defined the original. This roguelike shooter places you in control of a magical chicken warrior on a wild journey through vibrant and unpredictable stages filled with hordes of bizarre creatures. The game’s unapologetically chaotic combat and staggering number of build possibilities make it a standout in the genre, inviting players to dive into a world where creativity and skill must collide to survive. The gameplay centers on top-down, fast-paced combat where players face waves of enemies with a dazzling array of spells crafted from hundreds of magical components. What truly sets Machick 2 apart is the wand crafting system, which offers an astonishing level of customization—over a billion possible wand combinations. This depth allows players to tailor their combat style to nearly any preference, whether that’s unleashing rapid-fire projectiles, explosive blasts, or defensive shields. Alongside this, the inclusion of 24 skills with multiple evolutionary paths means that each run feels fresh and strategic, as you refine your build to tackle increasingly challenging foes. Combat encounters are intense and demand quick reflexes as well as thoughtful adaptation. Enemies come in a wide variety, each boasting unique behaviors and attack patterns that force you to adjust your tactics on the fly. The game doesn’t shy away from ramping up the difficulty, especially in boss battles that test your mastery of your chosen spells and skills. These epic confrontations stand out as highlights, requiring you to leverage your fully optimized loadout while navigating complex attack sequences and environmental hazards. Beyond combat, Machick 2 impresses with its extensive content. There are over 100 accessories available that can dramatically alter gameplay, ranging from changes in spell effects to modifications in movement and passive abilities. These accessories encourage experimentation, letting you discover powerful synergies and personalized strategies. The addition of active relics and legendary wands further diversifies the options, injecting moments of thrilling power spikes that can turn the tide of battle. Each of the eight unique stages is packed with secrets and environmental challenges that add layers of depth and replayability. Visually, the game embraces a colorful pixel art style that balances charm with clarity. The hand-drawn animations and vibrant effects bring the chaotic world to life, with spellcasting and explosions delivering satisfying visual feedback that complements the frantic gameplay without overwhelming the player. The quirky character designs and humorous touches permeate the atmosphere, reinforcing the game’s lighthearted and playful tone despite its challenging nature. In terms of accessibility, Machick 2 does a commendable job. The controls are intuitive, with customizable keybinds that cater to different play styles and preferences. The tutorial system is helpful for onboarding new players, ensuring the complex mechanics don’t become a barrier. The game also supports multiple languages, widening its appeal and allowing a global audience to jump in and enjoy the mayhem. Cloud saves and achievements integrated through Steam add to the overall polished experience, offering convenience and extra goals for completionists. Overall, Machick 2 is a robust and thoroughly entertaining roguelike shooter that excels in blending frenetic action with deep customization and a distinct sense of humor. It manages to strike a balance between accessibility and complexity, making it appealing to both newcomers and genre veterans. The sheer variety of builds and replayable content ensures that no two playthroughs are the same, keeping the gameplay engaging over the long haul. For anyone looking for a wildly creative and challenging roguelike with a unique twist, Machick 2 is a highly recommended adventure that promises chaotic fun and satisfying progression at every turn. Rating: 8/10

Another survival roguelite that could've been very good if not for the very poor in-game information. The Wand system is interesting and promises some very stupid combos (you know, the kind of thing we all play these games for). 4 parts make up each wand, 6 options each, each with its own interesting effects. The weapons are nothing revolutionary, but they're interesting and fun. Level them 8ish times and then evolve into one of three options. Characters.. well.. there are a lot of them, I can at least say that, but after close to 7 hours I still haven't found a single one. The only thing the game tells you is "Find in <Zone name>". Okay..? Well a dozen runs and 7 hours later and I'm still lookin. Roguelite progression is weak. You get 10 Stars after clearing a stage you haven't cleared before, and gold throughout the stage. Stars used for the usual stat progression, and gold is used to unlock wand parts. Stats.. exist. But what they do, how much I have? Your guess is as good as mine.

Beat the first stage on first try easily with starter wand. Proceeded to second stage expecting a moderate ramp up in difficulty. Instead I get killed every run by an unavoidable boulder that covers literally the entire screen. You can't outrun it and by the time you see it spawning its already too late. You've got to be kidding.

The game is nice, the art is pretty, has a funny storyline and character. The wand build system is cool (but goes back on the "too easy" aspect, where it really doesnt matter how you build them), the skill system is underwhelming.

I've only dipped my toes in for a few hours so far, but it's been great fun. The wand creation is neat and helpful, the graphics mean my potato PC can play it, the gameplay loop feels fun, and it's not frustrating with overlong animations or interruptions that make the flow of the game feel jarring. I did read a review that it was too easy, but unless I'm just too much of a neanderthal, I've found it to be challenging without me tearing my hair out. I'm glad I found this title. :) Update: I've clocked in about 15 hours but I think imma give it a rest for now until a big update drops; at the moment, I've gained waaay too much gold and stars to far outstrip the requirements for all the upgrades. It's fun, don't get me wrong; the balance just seems to be off in the player's favor a little too much. Still recommended, tho.

I will say the first 4 hours for me had me stuck on the first level till I figured out all the leveling up and once I did that I started to really push through the content and its overall great. Love the Frog vs Chicken concept and it works with great visuals humor and bosses. Some work could be done on the Hub and UI as it can be VERY difficult to read some elements on a handheld PC but style wise I love it. The hub can be annoying and wish some games just used good menus rather than walking around for no reason to each area. A proper stat or profile page would be appreciated as well. Devs are active and add some serious content from time to time as well. If you are a fan of Survivor Like games I can 100% recommend this gem... you will not be let down. Put some time into it and the light bulb will fire up and you wont be able to stop.

[h1]什么，鸡哥我竟与蛙蛙全族为敌？还好我会魔法！ [/h1] [h2]前言：[/h2] 成为一只小鸡，使用各种绚烂的魔法去击败邪恶的蛙蛙一族，从普通蛙蛙一路打到蛙之神。里面可以打造自己的魔杖还可以自由取名真是太酷了，我直接起手造一把【火之高兴】，游戏整体是吸血鬼幸存者的模式，有好几种局外成长，目前玩下来感觉上手很简单，手感还可以，数值欠打磨了一点。 [h2]玩法： [/h2] ※强烈建议去设置里打开【自动攻击】、【自动瞄准】，可以节约超多鼠标耐久。还可以打开宝箱加速刷新，可以刷新更多的宝箱获取更多道具饰品。 扮演一只会魔法的小鸡，使用各种魔杖攻击，魔杖可以自由打造或者在游戏里达成目标解锁几种传奇魔杖。魔杖的打造图纸、木头原材料、符文等等都需要花金币来解锁。 游戏里可以获取各种小鸡仔来帮助自己战斗，可以发射各种攻击弹幕或者帮忙产生效果，比如产出金币、帮忙收集掉落之类的。 然后进入战斗就是幸存者游戏的经典超大无限地图，一群各式各样的蛙会冲过来攻击，击败他们就可以了。 地图上会随机刷新出一些宝箱和道具，比如【金币宝箱】开启可以获得金币、【饰品宝箱】开启可以获得饰品产生加成和效果，打败杀马特头发的【独角蛙】可以掉落【遗物宝箱】开启可以获得【神明遗物雕像碎片】，集齐就可以装备雕像效果，【黑色诅咒宝箱】可以全图石化诅咒。此外还有一些地点道具，比如【鸡舍】可以获得2只普通小鸡仔，【鸡窝】可以获取一个随机的鸡蛋，可以孵出对应的小鸡仔。 有几率遇到彩蛋的九个连续【鸡窝】，会出现呈现一圈围住的9个鸡窝，直接可以爽吃9个蛋，孵出9个小鸡（如果是生蛋鸡就可以18只，直接开局就无敌了） 游戏中会随着捡起经验后升级获得技能，目前最多是4个技能槽位，可以获得四种不同的技能。技能总共是20级，每五次升级就是一个大升级，那个大升级的效果会更好一点。把技能升满就会触发进化技能的选项，可以二选一进化这个满级技能。如果把4种技能都升级满，接下来再升级就会获得基础属性的加强词条，比如提升攻击、提升金币获取率、提升经验获取倍率等等。 在地图里击杀一定数量的蛙蛙，会完成望远镜给的点数任务，给予一定数量的成长点书，然后回到基地之后就可以往上走去望远镜点局外成长，建议最开始先把移速和冲刺cd给点了。后面点数多了就随便点了。 [h2]小技巧： [/h2] 一个地图通关一次之后会解锁自定义模式，可以在里面把关卡调整为无尽模式，然后进去呆个几十分钟，出来之后的点数就可以点满成长树了。 潘多拉的魔盒非常强，尤其是在无尽模式里，怪多了之后全地图的几秒钟恐惧很好用。 饰品里面的【恶魔钥匙】也很强，效果是【黑色诅咒宝箱】可以升一级，效果刚开始看有点不明所以，实则是你开【黑色诅咒宝箱】就可以直接无视经验值升级，在等级高了经验获取需求大了之后非常强力，而且可以叠加，多个钥匙之后开一下就是好几级。 尽快解锁新的鸡角色，比如第二个角色【生蛋鸡】，孵化一个鸡蛋可以获得两只小鸡仔。直接几十只鸡仔，靠他们来打伤害。 [h2]吐槽和建议：[/h2] 1、光效太华丽，导致后期很容易卡顿，尤其是技能cd叠的很短，小鸡仔又很多的时候。 不得不开启性能模式了，感觉还可以再优化一下。。。 2、技能目前的强弱明显，有些技能基本不会去选。而且升级20级有点又臭又长，正常对局根本升不满，无尽模式升满又感觉只有2个进化方向太少了。 感觉可以给技能出多一点分支，缩短一点前置升级。 3、魔杖设计图纸没有演示动画，只能买下来做一把去实验才知道是什么效果，那些文字描述什么几个粒子几个魔法球啥的太不直观了。 感觉可以加个示范动画，这个图纸做出来的是什么攻击效果，而不是让人盲买。 4、感觉目前的技能间完全没有组合和配合，完全就是cd好了各打各的。 感觉可以做出那种不同的技能可以羁绊组合技或者进化新方向之类的。 [h2]总结：[/h2] 类幸存者玩法的游戏，化身魔法小鸡暴揍蛙蛙一族，可以打造属于自己的魔杖，也可以使用各种魔法技能，特效很华丽。在游戏里还可以随着任务目标的达成来逐步解锁局外成长、神明遗物雕像、新的小鸡角色、传奇魔杖等等新玩法。目前技能间没有组合且升级太过冗长，玩到5-10h以后会有些无聊。 [quote]欢迎关注鉴赏家: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/DCYXJLB] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url] 欢迎加入Steam组:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45300930] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url]来一起感受游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也可以顺手点个赞哟[/quote]

[b]MACHICK 2[/b], is a huge step up from Machick 1, instead of feeling like a rushed flash game, this is a full fleshed out survivors-like. The game has gone through major changes but somethings stay core to it. The lore is developed through a very charming flipbook-style animation, and whilst being simple, it is more than enough for this type of genre. The bosses were a big surprise as some of them completely change the stage/arena and are often than not 3D, which lets them stand out a lot from the normal gameplay loop. The game revolves around crafting wands that serve as your main auto-attack, and various standalone spells to cast during the runs. The game is a little buggy and poorly optimised even when early into endless. However, most of this can be worked around and don't disrupt the gameplay... too much. Each of the chicken are very unique and can focus on different builds. Don't expect there to be a long endgame like others of the genre though. Metaprogression runs out quickly and there is little replayability after you finish the story. There is plenty of references and fun items to try too. [b]PROS[/b]: - Interesting characters - Quirky animaltions - 3D models - Impressive spells and items - Little grinding [b]CONS[/b]: - Buggy - Poorly optomised - Minimal replayability [i]This is seriously much much better than the original game, what a difference a single year could make.[/i]
